title: Diagnostic biomarkers of neurodevelopmental and mental health disorders in children and adolescents
summary: Neurodevelopmental and mental health disorders, such as ADHD, autism, selective mutism and social anxiety, typically manifest during childhood or adolescence. Many of the symptoms overlap, such as difficulties with social interactions and pronounced anxiety. This often makes accurate diagnosis difficult. So far, diagnosis has been based mainly on interviews, questionnaires, and clinical impressions, all of which can be subjectively influenced. The planned study aims to identify objective biological measures ('biomarkers') that can support diagnosis. To this end, electrical brain activity at rest will be measured using an electroencephalogram (EEG). In patients with ADHD, symptoms and related dysfunctions will be additionally investigated in an experimental task of working memory, both behavioral and neurophysiological (using reaction times, response behavior and EEG). The EEG is a simple, inexpensive and well-tolerated method. The obtained brain data is evaluated using modern methods. The aim is to establish whether specific patterns of brain activity can distinguish between different disorders. In the long term, this could lead to faster, more objective and precise diagnoses in everyday clinical practice.

interventions.name: Patients aged 6–17 years with a confirmed diagnosis of ADHD undergo resting-state EEG examination and experimental task
Patients aged 6–17 years with a confirmed diagnosis of autism spectrum disorder undergo resting-state EEG examination
Patients aged 6–17 years with a confirmed diagnosis of social anxiety disorder undergo resting-state EEG examination
Patients aged 6–17 years with a confirmed diagnosis of mutism undergo resting-state EEG examination
Healthy subjects aged 6–17 years undergo resting-state EEG examination

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
A confirmed diagnosis of ADHD, ASD, mutism or social anxiety disorder, as defined by the ICD-10 or DSM-5
No diagnosis of a comorbid neuropsychiatric developmental disorder
An IQ of at least average
Exclusion criteria:
IQ <85
Diagnosis of comorbid neuropsychiatric developmental disorder
